back: Pale blue ppt with both; insoluble in excess NaOH; dissolves in excess NH₃ to a dark blue solution.

front: Hydroxides that dissolve in excess NaOH(aq)
back: Al³⁺, Zn²⁺, Cr³⁺ (dark green solution) and Pb²⁺ (ZIMSEC): amphoteric hydroxides.
Fe²⁺: green ppt, turns brown on standing (oxidised by air). Fe³⁺: red-brown ppt. Both insoluble in excess.
AgCl white (soluble in dilute NH₃); AgBr cream (partially soluble); AgI pale yellow (insoluble).
Acidify (dilute HCl or HNO₃), add Ba²⁺(aq): white ppt of BaSO₄, insoluble in excess acid. Never acidify with H₂SO₄.
Warm with NaOH(aq) and Al foil: NH₃ given off, turns damp red litmus blue. (Nitrite does the same.)
NH₃: damp red litmus blue. CO₂: limewater milky. Cl₂: bleaches damp litmus. H₂: pops. O₂: relights glowing splint. SO₂: acidified dichromate orange → green.

front: Ca²⁺ and Ba²⁺ with the alkalis
back: No ppt with NH₃(aq). NaOH(aq): white ppt with Ca²⁺ (unless very dilute), little or none with Ba²⁺.
Observation: 'effervescence; gas turned limewater milky'. Deduction: 'CO₂, so carbonate present'.
Both: white ppt soluble in excess NaOH, insoluble in NH₃. Pb²⁺ gives white PbCl₂ with Cl⁻ and yellow PbI₂ with I⁻.
